reviews.title: Offer of Free Month Charged me Immediately
reviews.text:
I have tried insight timer on and off for years.  I absolutely despise all the hoop jumping to get to the main menu… all my goals, and consecutive days, and good job; super tedious and unnecessary. The user interface is super confusing as well; no easy way to see what you like, your playlists etc. 

Recently, I was looking for something specific and went back on it to see if they had what I wanted.  While I was there it offered me a free month, so I thought, that’s generous, why not? So I agreed. 

 Within minutes my card was charged for year and no free month. Guess who has to then figure out how to request a refund?  

I did this through both apple and insight timer.  Insight timer offered no help, and no month free, just a lot of words of concern.  Apple did, after 24 hours, refund my money, but I also lost my supposed free month.  

Be wary. What a total waste of time.

reviews.title: Stupid log in
reviews.text: I already have a PAID account and every time I have to sign it the app requires you to go through an onboarding process.  Why?

reviews.title: Used to be amazing
reviews.text: The video content and worse the auto playing of it. Is ridiculous for the supposed intention of this app. Took a once peaceful tool and turned it into another social media attention seeking app

reviews.title: Keeps getting Worse…
reviews.text:
Latest Update someone named “Christopher” is overriding my system settings and autoplaying in a video speaking. 

If my music stops and i hit play again, I get Christopher again, not my music. 

When a track ends my practice is interrupted again with a celebration that I use the app every day - thanks - I know?! .. the celebration cannot be turned off or bypassed to access the next track.. 

Their solution was to continue quitting the app and restarting lol why not resolve these issues? 

I have been wondering which device was malfunctioning for 3 days now. I don’t listen to audio speaking. Yet a have a random man’s voice coming through my speakers unexpectedly in my home, alarming me, rather than allowing me to relax, and meditate - which was once the whole point of this app.

reviews.title: Intrusive Questioning
reviews.text:
This review is specifically about the intrusive questions and apparent use of AI to “design a programme”.  Most importantly, the fact that you cannot use the app without completing a long list of questions is unacceptable.
For an app that is promoting trauma-informed practice, this lack of consent and choice is out of integrity.  Personally, I clicked through any old answers just to use the app, so the questions were useless and the AI process wasted resources creating a meaningless plan. 

Please make this process consensual with the option to opt out.

reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: This app literally saved my life. But the past couple of weeks have frustrated me to the point of deleting the app. Constant updates so you can’t find anything, video summaries instead of written (everytime I open the app, I am bombarded with these videos) and now having to pay for meditations. Such a shame it became all about money.

reviews.title: Stop the gamification of meditation
reviews.text: I have subscribed to Insight Timer for more than 10 years. I used to love it. Now, logging on requires me to answer 1 million questions about my goals and interests. It wants to set up targets and competitions and reminders. I just want to freaking meditate. What used to be the most straightforward meditation app became the biggest three ring circus and I couldn’t be more disappointed. I’m sure it makes the developers more money this way, so enjoy.

reviews.title: Suddenly freezing
reviews.text: Complete ceasefire on app access

reviews.title: Turn off commitment/milestone nonsense
reviews.text:
I wish this app would just not waste 20s after every single meditation with “you have hit your 5th milestone - gold star”. “Are you ready to commit to 14 days?” “Choose your commitment”. 
Just let people meditate in peace without needing to do all this nonsense and your slow visualizations wasting my time. I have to hit 7 buttons just to be able to end a meditation. 

Or at least build an option to turn it all off and just use a timer without being bothered!

reviews.title: Can’t stand it anymore
reviews.text: Doesn’t properly track your usage then resets your streaks incorrectly daily now. So unbelievably aggravating it is the exact opposite of relaxing and even more mind blowing for an app supposedly based around soothing you, you literally can’t even just fully turn off this gamification!!!! As soon as my subscription is done I won’t renew sadly after many years using. Contacted support multiple times and they are beyond useless and doing nothing to resolve this clear fundamental fault.

reviews.title: Almost the best meditation app

reviews.title: Shoulds, shame, and gamefication

If I pick it up to meditate, I can’t just go into the library- I am forced to click through half a dozen irritating popups about how great the app is and everything I SHOULD be doing everyday. Just let me meditate! Not everything needs to be social media!

reviews.title: Frustrating updates

reviews.title: Can’t cancel

reviews.title: Hate the update

The point of this app has been grounding and getting away from those kinds of things in life where we cannot escape them. Terrible to have added them here. Hate hate hate hate that I can no longer listen to a brief preview in the list screen, cannot believe it forces me to go to a detail screen and tries to get me stuck in a scroll of other previews. A truly repulsive approach. Were you recently purchased by PE or something?

reviews.title: Wastes your time with forced engagement
reviews.text: Used to use this app daily.  Then they started forcing engagement with questions and emotion check ins. These are obnoxious and time wasting.  Only get this app if you want to lose time daily to a wellness corporation.

reviews.title: Really pushy agenda makes the app terrible to use, wish that wasn’t the case
reviews.text: The app is incredibly frustrating to use due to its relentless efforts to categorize users, push them to set up schedules and goals whether they want to or not, and then shower them with unwanted screens asking them to say “I’m committed” and engage with the product every day.  Once in a great while, I’ll use the app for something specific.  But I almost don’t even want to try!  The experience outside of the actual teaching is so bad for me.  Check out other reviews to see what I mean.  I would want to give the app 3 stars because I’ve benefited from it.  But the fact that Insight Timer doesn’t listen to feedback and change their ways means I’m going to leave a 1 star review with the goal of having more impact on the overall rating.

reviews.title: Let us skip intro questions

reviews.title: Too gamified for me
reviews.text: I have a few meditation apps and this one is by far the most gamified, mainstream, over produced one. I dont care about streaks, i just want the ability to open an app, pick a session, and listen to it. Its also very controlling. You can’t rewind in a session unless youre a paid subscriber. I suppose it could be a good gateway app but if youre serious about mindfulness you will likely move on (and be happy about it) when you get sick of this one’s annoying features. Its a meditation app for pop culture.

reviews.title: Stop with the pop ups

reviews.title: Rewinding is a paid feature now??? Adios Insight Timer
reviews.text:
Tl;dr: This app has become unusable at the free tier. And I refuse to use/support this app as long as this is the pay-to-play business model being implemented. 

(details in full review below) 

I’ve always enjoyed this app. And I saw value in the premium features. But it used to still be of value to the free users. 
Making it a thing that Rewind and Time Scrub/Timestamp Selection are a pay to play thing takes a LOT away from free users. 
After meditations, I would often go back to certain spots and listen to key words/moments so I could remember important stuff I wanted/needed to journal about. 
With my brain traumas, this had become an integral part of any guided meditations. 

I haven’t used apps for meditation for a while, and am looking to get an app again for it. 

This app ain’t it. 
Y’all are taking stuff away from people who need it and may not have the means to pay for premium. So even when I have the means to go premium, I won’t. Because I refuse to support this business model.

reviews.title: Insight into Gamification
reviews.text: I used this app for many years when it was just a simple timer. I was very happy with its clean interface, sounds and ease of use. Then, it went all infantile and gamified: stats, check-ins, streaks, etc. Even in a practice like meditation, you can't be distracted from distraction by the distraction these app developers insist upon. Very depressing.

reviews.title: So difficult to find anything

I listen to the same handful of meditations now because it’s designed in a way that is too aggravating to explore or even find content on a specific topic. Even finding meditations I previously listened to is a nightmare scrolling exercise now - the irony of being frustrated using an app intended to help you relax. Really disappointing to see the user experience deteriorate so much., it used to be one of my favorite apps.

reviews.title: cancelling my subscription
reviews.text: insight app used to be my gold standard meditation app, but every update makes it less like a meditation app and more like a social media platform. Ever since they added the video feature, when you open the app instead of calming images, you now get awful aggressively extroverted self-promoting headshots. This engagement attempt visually jarring and I’m using this app less and less because I can’t stand opening it and seeing these thumbnails anymore. There is no option to disable the video thumbs (and video feature) or customise the layout. It’s also poor taste and off-putting to demand a rating from paid subscribers and suggest tips immediately afterwards. All of these behaviours are counterintuitive to meditation.

reviews.title: Please stop making it more convoluted
reviews.text: This app used to be so simple, so clean and so easy to use. Now, I have to fumble through a bunch of features I don’t care about. This is a meditation and yoga app, not Pinterest for the soul. Why are “Editor’s picks” displayed prominently in two separate places? Why isn’t there an option to simply not to view those? Why isn’t there an option to clean up the view and disable the unwanted portions? The homepage isn’t even items I chose. Bookmarks and playlists should be on the homepage, as should events I signed up for. Signing up for a trial of Plus is also a headache too. It’s far too easy for Insight Timer to just charge you before your trial is up and it’s difficult to cancel membership. Please fix your app, stop giving people what they didn’t ask you for and make your app user friendly.

Also after a meditation session, you need to click so many buttons: Shall the session be marked as completed or rejected, rate the session, repeat the same session tomorrow or not, if not it opens a screen to pick a different session for next day… it’s very limiting your free choice, forcing you into unwanted interactions by locking the screen until you made a decision and preventing a quick return to the main screen of the app - VERY annoying and pushy.

reviews.title: Bigger isn’t better
reviews.text: Still no way to mark the tracks or teachers I don’t like. Bigger isn’t better. Update: Did I just get a pop up about new live yoga right after I started my meditation timer? Yes. Yes, I did. Um, can’t the ads wait until after I’ve done my sitting practice? Updated review: some of the changes are good, but I think now that I've been using guided meditations more I've noticed places for improvement. First - it no longer switches to landscape view on the iPad - that's a small thing but it used to so now it's just frustrating. More importantly, to get to my bookmarked meditations, I have to go through something like 5 screens, many of them with very bright white backgrounds. In the dark morning this is very off putting. Finally, still, no download option means you have to be connected to the internet. I still love Insight Timer. The changes are great! One thing I would change: you can't rate a guided mediation unless you listen all the way thru. This means that 1)of course all the ratings are high bc who's going to sit thru 60 minutes of a bad mediation to rate it? and 2) there's no way to track those I've tried and didn't like. I wish there was some way to track negative ones as well as good ones. Older: This app has really helped me develop a meditation routine. Very dedicated customer service.

reviews.title: Forcing video into my mindfulness practice? Absolutely not.
reviews.text:
As someone who works in media, I’m keenly aware of how insidious the “pivot to video” creep has become. My favorite meditation app was the last place I expected it to show up. 

I’ve been a dedicated Insight Timer user for over a decade. It’s where I go to unplug, ground myself and literally *close my eyes.* What’s kept me loyal to IT is how calming and low-stimulation the user experience is — it used to be so simple and practical, like the Reddit of meditation apps. I loved that it never really changed. So waking up one morning to find a carousel of *meditation videos* (who is asking for these, seriously?) suddenly featured at the top of the home screen, with no way to turn the feature off, feels manipulative and totally inconsistent with the app’s original purpose. Seeing so many faces staring back at me (with sleek, professional lighting and backgrounds) when I’ve opened the app specifically to get away from that vibe grosses me out, like self-improvement is being TikTokified.

Miss me with this redesign. If there truly is a demand for video content in this space (which I find hard to fathom), there are ways to meet it without forcing the rest of us to go down the scroll hole with you. I’m taking my meditation practice elsewhere, and I hope everyone serious about their practice does too.

But then after the meditation, the endless clicks, animations, and questions to get back out are infuriating, negating the effect of the session. Even worse, on a regular basis it replaces the “continue” button with an “install widget” button. Here’s a thought: if I wanted the widget I would have installed it by now. Why do you think trying to trick me into putting the widget onto my phone is a good idea? It makes me want to uninstall your app, not use it more.

The same stupid questions each time I open the app. Its a waste of time and detracts from my time meditating. This app is ruined.

reviews.title: Annoying questions
reviews.text: The timer is good but I’m so sick of getting annoying questions every time I open the app. I also don’t like that I need to commit to a time and number of data before using it when I know I’m just using the timer that day and do not want to commit to a daily practice. It feels like I need to lie just to use it.

reviews.title: I can’t stand this app
reviews.text:
The content is great, but the app itself is beyond annoying. 

I’m a paying subscriber and use the app occasionally, maybe every two weeks. Each time I open the app I’m bombarded with a series of prompts asking me how I’m feeling, what I’m aiming towards, what my motivation is, when I like to meditate, etc. All of which I need to answer before it allows me to access the content I’m paying for. There’s no option to ignore this and I’ve un-ticked every related setting for reminders, prompts and things within the app. 

Is it too much to ask to be able to access my paid content without all this unnecessary spam? It’s ironic that this ritual actually puts me in a more agitated state of mind than I was in before opening my mindfulness app. Perhaps it’s just a disingenuous way for the developers to harvest our data? If so, I can’t imagine that data’s of great quality, because I just mash through the closest answers to get the thing to go away. 

I hope they change this feature, because it’s unfair to the many incredibly talented practitioners who produce content for this app. But if they don’t change it soon, I’ll go elsewhere for my mindfulness content.

reviews.title: Sound Mixer not really working
reviews.text:
When you start their sound mixer, half of the sounds simply won’t’ download! I tried all tricks. Their customer
service is poor, just chatbot! Waste of money.

reviews.title: My opinion
reviews.text: I miss when the check ins were available as you start your session. I also miss the check ins motivating you based on your response such as- if you had a bad day it would tell you to keep going or it gets better ect. Now you have to go to a diffferent area to check in and get no reassurance

reviews.title: Frustrating transition from a simple tool to an intrusive experience
reviews.text:
I have been a dedicated user of Insight Timer since 2017, but I am writing this review out of pure frustration with the current state of the app. What used to be a straightforward, helpful tool for meditation has become incredibly intrusive.

My biggest issue is that the app has become nearly impossible to use without being forced through a gauntlet of questionnaires and "onboarding" tasks. I cannot simply open the app to meditate; I am bombarded with demands to set timers, create goals, and commit to practice schedules. I do not want AI guidance, I do not want accountability dashboards, and I do not want stickers or scores. I simply want to open the app, find my content, and practice in peace. Being forced to provide consent or answer questions just to access a timer is unacceptable.

Beyond the intrusive UI, the search and history functions are chaotic. The "Recently Used" list is cluttered and completely uneditable. There is no way to remove tracks I didn't enjoy, which means the list is constantly filled with content I don't want to see again. It should be a basic feature to be able to curate your own history so you aren't accidentally re-playing content that didn't resonate with you.

Overall, the app has become a cluttered, high-pressure environment when it should be the exact opposite. Please, provide an option for a "serene" mode—a simple, clean interface that allows users to open the app, do their practice, and get out without all the forced engagement, goals, and ch

reviews.title: Stop met plus pushen
reviews.text: Gebruik de app vrijwel dagelijks, fijn. Tot mijn teleurstelling komt er regelmatig een scherm waarop Plus aan wordt geraden. Ik heb echt al 10 keer “nee bedankt” gezegd. 1 keer moet echt genoeg zijn. Nee = nee. Dit werkt triggerend en dat is vast niet jullie bedoeling.

reviews.title: Te veel ruis
reviews.text: Elke dag krijg je nieuw aanbod onder je neus. Extreem veel keus, bijv 40 instrumenten/gongs bij de timer. Veel te veel ruis voor een app die innerlijke rust en groei als doel heeft.

reviews.title: Terrible customer service
reviews.text: Good luck getting help from the support team if your mental wellbeing is impacted by the app not working properly. I’ve had issues with meditations stopping mid-track and jumping back to random points.  They asked me for a bunch of information then blamed my connectivity that had nothing to do with it. App is full of unnecessary and annoying additions. Not what it used to be. Don’t bother subscribing

reviews.title: Waste of money
reviews.text: Trying to get a refund for this app is impossible.  No reminder of subscriptions is sent. No emails to check in for in active accounts.  Complete waste of money, time and opportunity.

reviews.title: Used to be good
reviews.text: Get rid of that stupid animation at the end of the timer meditation. So annoying.

reviews.title: App sadly ruined
reviews.text: I never write reviews usually, but very sad to finally be saying goodbye to this app after a decade of using it. The amount of unnecessary and unavoidable pop ups is ironically about as irritating and unmindful as possible for a meditation app. I just want to use the timer! I don’t want to commit to anything or tell you about my goals, ever!

reviews.title: Acts like a free service
reviews.text: Every time I do a meditation I am asked if I want to share my progress. I can’t move forward without hitting share or skip. I am sorry but in what world do you think I’d want to share my progress. Why would any one do that? How often is this feature actually used? As a user it is just in my way of getting on to the next meditation. As a paid service I don’t expect to get bothered by your attempts at self promotion.

reviews.title: "Ich bin entschlossen" - Nein, das bin ich nicht!
reviews.text: Ich habe alle Möglichkeiten zu Benachrichtigungen zur Motivation deaktiviert und trotzdem werde ich nach jeder Meditation mit Fragen belästigt ob ich ich entschlossen bin am nächsten Tag weiterzumachen. Das ärgert mich. Ich zahle gerne für diese App aber dieses Bedrängen lässt mich ein Verlängern des Abonnements in Frage stellen! Warum sind diese Meldungen nicht optional?

reviews.title: Library gone
reviews.text: Carefully built library of meditations for different situations gone with one update. Now replaced with teachers and meditation retreats, in which I have no interest. Super strange move that practically ruined the app for me.

reviews.title: Used to be so good before new management turned it into a money machine
reviews.text: Wow guys. This app used to be a place for honest reviews of great teachers and a simple interface that wasn't gunning for your wallet in inescapable 20 click surveys leading to a credit card payment.

reviews.title: Nervt immer mehr

Please cancel the subscription (£35) that I never asked for.   If I need this app, maybe I will subscribe. But it is not my case

We unfortunately have to use it as our child likes one of the story series on here, but just trying to open it up means going through a bunch of unskippable questions or prompts. It’s infuriating. Please just calm it down, using this app is a huge source of frustration. Is that irony?

reviews.title: Meditation nachtragen nicht möglich ☹️
reviews.text:
Leider kann man die Tage, an denen man meditiert hat, ohne die App zu aktivieren, nicht oder nur sehr begrenzt nachträglich eintragen. 👎
Wenn man  z.B. für zwei Tage, oder länger auf einem Retreat ist und dort meditiert, ohne die App zu nutzen, wird der Zähler der durchgehenden Tage einfach auf 0 gesetzt.
Hier würde ich mir mehr Vertrauen in die Nutzer:innen wünschen, eigenverantwortlich die Tage und Meditationszeiten, ohne Begrenzung nachträglich nachtragen zu können!

reviews.title: Very disappointing for a wellness app
reviews.text: I have tried to contact insight timer help a number of times and have not received a reply

reviews.title: App has become bloated and unusable
reviews.text: I’ve had this app for years and enjoyed the simple meditation timer and sometimes guided meditations. In the last few years it’s become bloated with features, prompts and endless screens you need to click through just to get to the timer. Even loading the app takes far longer now. I’m not sure who all these features are meant to serve but this app no longer supports a real meditation practice or mindful use of technology.

reviews.title: This is not free
reviews.text: I used to have this app and use it regularly but on downloading it this time it asked for a yearly subscription.

reviews.title: Why change a good app?
reviews.text: I use this app for the meditation timer. Haven’t used it for a while, now that I’ve returned it has some ridiculous tv static noise after the bells. There is no option to get rid of it. It’s set at no background noise but keeps doing it. So now I’m unsubscribing  and not paying any more money. Why do app creators continually ruin something that’s good?

reviews.title: (Not) insight timer
reviews.text: This app became everything a meditation timer app should not become. Opening a just updated version made me click 10 times to be able to just start the timer! Horrible experience.

reviews.title: Tolle App aber wehe du hast sie länger nicht genutzt
reviews.text: Ich nutze die App sehr gerne und finde sie im großen und Ganzen richtig toll. Da ich sie aber nicht regelmäßig öffne, kommt jedes Mal (!) der Startsceen zum Einrichten. Und ich frage mich warum? Klar ändern sich die eigenen Ziele und Intentionen und es ist schön, alles entsprechend neu einzurichten. Aber wenn ich die App öffne, will ich meditieren und nicht jedes Mal etwas einrichten müssen. Bitte ändert mal die Frequenz dessen, oder lasst einem die freie Wahl später, wenn man im Home Screen drin ist. Denn es ist echt nervig sich jedes Mal durch diese vielen Seiten durchzuklicken und zu warten, bis die App die passenden Meditationen rausgesucht hat.

reviews.title: Wow. My review was removed!
reviews.text: Already given feedback twice about the pop ups being the antithesis to zen and supporting neurodivergence. Seems you don’t want to know, or respond. Disappointing

reviews.text:
Gut gemacht aber leider viel zu umständlich. Wer einen simplen gong timer sucht ist hier falsch. Viel zu viele geklicke und werbung für die in App Käufe. 
War früher besser und hab den tracker sehr geschätzt. Jetzt leider bur 2 sterne

reviews.title: Stop with the questions!
reviews.text: Everytime i try do get into a maditation session i have to answer like 20 questions and skip past 5 monetization options. Just stop it ffs. Most people just want to use the timer, its not that deep!

reviews.title: In-app prompts are a put off
reviews.text: I contacted the app developers late last year, no reply yet, about my experience of the prompts you can’t ignore, in that instance the ‘spotification’ / end of year data about how much I’d used the app. I explained why it’s a put off for me, it’s not neurodiversity friendly (PDA), and I’d searched long and hard in the app to find where to turn these notifications off so really didn’t appreciate multiple screens you have to go through (no opt out), thinking each was the last screen and not knowing how long this was going to go for, before you can use the app. After weeks of not using the app because of this very issue, I log on to see it’s happened again! This time, ‘welcome back’ followed by another 7 screens I can’t opt out of before I can even use the app. Between this and no reply to my contact, I am inclined to delete the app and cancel my subscription. Offering me a choice then ignoring my preference means this isn’t a safe place to go to when I need to calm my brain. I’d argue that neurodiverse people need meditation more than the average person, but we also need you to listen and grow when we give feedback. As it stands, I’ve paid for a service I now can’t use, and which doesn’t even acknowledge the gems in the feedback I provided.

reviews.title: Used to be perfect, now incredibly bloated
reviews.text: Thoroughly enjoyed the old app which just was a simple timer and maybe some extras. Now you have to click no to 7-10 pop-ups before you can start your meditation. Incredibly frustrating and very much not in line with the essence of the app. Please stop being so profit hungry, accept that you have created a beautiful app without the bloat, focus on a simple premium package that actually delivers value and invest your time in other things. Not everything needs to generate immense profits

reviews.title: Werbung, werbung, werbung
reviews.text: Man möchte die App zum meditieren verwenden und wird mit Werbung überschwemmt. War mal ne gute App. Mittlerweile unbrauchbar

reviews.title: Tolle App mit großem ABER
reviews.text: Die App bietet eine riesige Auswahl zur Begleitung und Unterstützung bei der Meditation und da ist für jeden was dabei - ob Musik, sphärische Klänge, Naturgeräusche, mit oder ohne Anleitung - das ist fantastisch. Jetzt kommt das Aber: was echt nervt, sind die vielen Fragen. Wenn man die App zB. nach einer Weile das erste mal wieder öffnet, muss man sich schier endlos durchklicken, bis man endlich einfach nur meditieren kann. Auch nach der Meditation, da sind mir einfach zu viele Fragen und Angaben durch die man sich klicken muss. Das nervt mich massiv und ich habe noch keine Möglichkeit gefunden das abzustellen.
